original_question: Does every subgroup of a solvable group have bounded packing, in the sense that for every radius r > 0 there is a uniform bound N after which any N distinct left cosets must contain a pair whose distance is at least r in a proper left-invariant metric on the group?
target_in_paper: The bounded-packing statement nearest to your draft is the paper’s special-case result corresponding to Theorem 1.3: for the semidirect product P_{n,φ} = ℤ^n ⋊_φ ℤ, if φ ∈ Aut(ℤ^n) is diagonalizable and all eigenvalues of φ are real, then every subgroup of P_{n,φ} has bounded packing. This is presented in the paper as progress toward the motivating virtually polycyclic bounded-packing question, not as a statement about all solvable groups.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly states the bounded-packing condition itself: for each radius r > 0 there should be a uniform bound on the size of a family of distinct left cosets that are all mutually close, equivalently any sufficiently large family of distinct left cosets contains a pair at distance at least r. It also correctly uses a proper left-invariant metric.
missing_details: The paper does not formulate this as a question about all solvable groups. In the nearby introductory context, the motivating ambient class is virtually polycyclic groups, and the theorem actually proved is for the special semidirect products P_{n,φ} = ℤ^n ⋊_φ ℤ.
The ambient group must be specified explicitly as P_{n,φ} = ℤ^n ⋊_φ ℤ.
The automorphism φ must be specified as an element of Aut(ℤ^n).
The theorem requires φ to be diagonalizable.
The theorem also requires all eigenvalues of φ to be real.
The subgroup quantified over is an arbitrary subgroup H ≤ P_{n,φ}.
The cosets in the bounded-packing definition are distinct left cosets of H.
The distance between cosets should be understood as the set distance d(gH, g'H) = inf{ d(gh, g'h') : h, h' ∈ H }.
The nearby formal definition in the paper is stated for finitely generated groups with the word metric, together with the remark that this is equivalent to using any proper left-invariant metric.

A paper-specific nuance missing from the draft is the reduction idea behind Proposition 1.2: in these semidirect products, the cyclic subgroup coming from the ℤ-factor is the essential case from which bounded packing for arbitrary subgroups is deduced.
refined_question: Let P_{n,φ} = ℤ^n ⋊_φ ℤ, where φ ∈ Aut(ℤ^n) is diagonalizable and all eigenvalues of φ are real. Does every subgroup H ≤ P_{n,φ} have bounded packing in P_{n,φ}; that is, for every r > 0, is there an N = N(P_{n,φ}, H, r) such that any collection of N distinct left cosets of H contains two cosets whose distance is at least r (equivalently, not all pairwise distances are < r), with respect to any proper left-invariant metric on P_{n,φ}?
justification: The draft gets the geometry of bounded packing essentially right, but it broadens the ambient class too far: the bounded-packing part of this paper is not about arbitrary solvable groups. In the introduction to the bounded-packing section, the motivating question is whether every subgroup of a virtually polycyclic group has bounded packing, and the concrete class studied is P_{n,φ} = ℤ^n ⋊_φ ℤ, described as the simplest non-abelian polycyclic examples. The main result proved there is that every subgroup of P_{n,φ} has bounded packing when φ is diagonalizable with real eigenvalues. The nearby context also supplies the formal bounded-packing definition, the metric-independence remark, and the reduction perspective that the ℤ-factor subgroup is the essential case. So the sharp paper-faithful rewrite is the P_{n,φ} question above, not the broader solvable-group version.
